items.summary_1line: Gemini 4 Argon went GA today, but we already gave it title story 2 weeks ago and most benchmarks, like CursorBench, simply independently confirm their claims.
items.editor_note: Reports GA and says independent benchmarks like CursorBench confirm Google's claims.

editorial.tldr: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Argon on Sep 30 as its next frontier model. Latent Space framed it a day later as DeepMind's answer to Astra and Fable, with 1M output tokens, but only Fairwind Program users could try it.
editorial.whats_new: Gemini 4 Argon went generally available on Oct 14, a day after reaching Google Cloud, with Latent Space noting that independent benchmarks such as CursorBench so far confirm Google's claims.
editorial.why_it_matters: GA plus Google Cloud availability means you can price and test Argon today, and early independent numbers match the launch claims; the 1M output limit matters for long agent runs.
editorial.take_for_builders: Run a small eval of Argon on Google Cloud against your pinned Gemini model and record cost per completed task before changing any default; check your own workload, since the independent confirmations so far are benchmark-based.

status.detail: Announced Sep 30 with restricted access; Google Cloud availability and safety documentation followed Oct 13, and GA was reported Oct 14.
